tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

reservoir-computing-definition-fixed-net: Introduction: the page describes what its reservoir computer is and states the key difference, fixed network with a trained output layer.
qci-info-dits-qudits: Bits and dits: the page defines a dit as a system with d configurations and names the quantum terms qubit and qudit.
qci-info-photon-qudit-limit: How much information can a light particle store?: the page states the formula assumes measurements that would be very difficult in practice and a computer that can use them.
qci-info-multi-dof-difficult: Computing with light particles in practice: the page states multi-degree-of-freedom encoding is likely difficult for a real device and says why.
qci-photons-page-is-overview: Further reading: the page says 'This page is a high-level overview' and links deeper work; the page text contains no experiments or proofs.
zeno-page-conceptual-scope: Opening paragraph: the page states it explains at a conceptual level without the full mathematics and points to a separate article for the rigorous mathematics.
zeno-observing-definition: Introduction: 'Here observing is a loose term' defines the word as strongly interacting with something else.
zeno-blockade-definition: Introduction: the page names the effect of making two photons bounce off each other the Zeno blockade.
optical-cavity-resonance-definition: Optical Cavity: the page defines resonance as fitting a full number of wavelengths. The multi-frequency clause is a plain physics statement attached to it.
cavity-hamiltonian-coupling: Optical Cavity: the page writes this Hamiltonian as its own model with c defined as the entry rate.
sum-frequency-generation-definition: Sum-frequency Generation: the page defines the process it uses as two photons combining into one at the sum frequency.
blockade-model-all-resonant: Simplified Zeno Blockade: the page states its model assumes resonance with s, i and p, calls this hard to engineer, and says loss would complicate the equation.
blockade-description-simplified: Real Zeno Blockade: the page states its description is highly simplified and that there are several complications.
blockade-large-G-hard: Real Zeno Blockade: the page states making G large is hard because the nonlinear effects are weak, and that fields must be confined to small regions.

theory_low.qci-info-wavelength-tradeoff: A vendor tutorial statement of physics with no derivation or measurement in the page; a field statement. Stated as a tradeoff, not derived.

theory_low.qci-info-photon-qudit-dimension: A formula the page itself says to take with a big grain of salt; no derivation, built on unproved independence of four degrees of freedom.
theory_low.cavity-transfer-time: Stated as a consequence with no derivation in the page; a field statement.
theory_low.strong-G-prevents-entry: Stated in one sentence with no derivation here; the argument in Simplified Zeno Blockade is informal. Not a proved result.
theory_low.blockade-empty-cavity-no-effect: An informal argument from the form of the Hamiltonian terms, not a stated and proved theorem; a theoretical claim.
theory_low.blockade-intermediate-regime: The page says only that results will be messy; no calculation or proof.
theory_low.blockade-weak-nonlinearity-regime: A one-line informal claim, no derivation or proof in the page.
theory_low.blockade-strong-regime-mechanism: An informal amplitude argument; the page only shows animations. Not a proved result, and the conditions are loose.
theory_low.blockade-sign-cancellation: An informal sign argument ('it turns out'); no derivation, and the page itself says the lossy case is more complicated.
theory_low.blockade-gate-sign-claim: An informal statement that the sign can be used for quantum gates; no derivation and the page says this is not quite how it uses the blockade.
